target_customer: Founders of German companies, fintech and accounting partners (Qonto, Sevdesk) embedding company formation, and businesses needing register data
problem: Founding a GmbH or UG in Germany takes weeks of notary and register paperwork.
business_model: Per formation fees plus subscription services and API access for partners
product_category: Legaltech, online company formation and notarial platform

founders.name: Alexander Sporenberg
founders.background_notes: YC page says he was on the founding team at Razor Group and led 150 plus M&A transactions.

founders.name: Felix Gerlach
previous_startups: Passbase Inc. (B2B KYC and AML SaaS, exited 2023)
founders.background_notes: Education not given on the YC page.

technical_complexity.rationale: Automating notary video appointments, document generation and Handelsregister filing through APIs needs integration with German notary and register systems, standard engineering with regulatory complexity.

defensibility.rationale: Notary and register integrations plus embedded partner distribution (Qonto, Sevdesk) are harder to copy than a front end, but other formation sites already existed.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Qonto became a partner rather than a rival, and Openlaw bought insolvent firma.de in June 2026 and agreed to buy registercheck.de in September 2026.

market_need_then: German company formation took 6 to 8 weeks according to the company; the online notary procedure had recently become possible for GmbH formation.

branding.domain_note: Uses the .de domain beglaubigt.de, the German word for certified; the parent company brand is Openlaw.

identity.voice_and_tone: Practical and service oriented: formation in days, 25,000 plus customers

branding.brand_signature: One engine, three brands: Beglaubigt.de, firma.de, Registercheck.de

brand_strength.rationale: A literal German legal word is clear to the local market but hard to spell and say for non Germans; the group now uses the Openlaw umbrella.

outcome_analysis: Openlaw runs Beglaubigt.de and reports over 25,000 customers and embedded partners like Qonto and Sevdesk. It closed a 3.3 million dollar seed in April 2026, then bought firma.de out of insolvency in June 2026 and agreed to buy registercheck.de in September 2026, funded from its own cash. Partner distribution and experienced founders explain the traction; there is no exit.
notes: Seed of 3.3M (2.8M euro) April 2026 reported by Munich Startup, tech.eu and Startbase in search results; the investor list varies by outlet and one outlet mislabels it Series A. Munich Startup's profile lists a separate 130K YC investment in September 2024, a single source and not recorded as a round. The company website fetch was blocked by a rate limited safety check, so site content comes from search snippets. Competitor search found only 2026 price pages (Qonto, firma.de, online.notar.de), so the founding era list is empty. Founder education not found.
